statuses.title: Loss-scale backoff/growth is an unaccounted data-dependent adaptive choice
statuses.note: Resolved by 7f55aae5 delete(engine)!: remove data-dependent loss scaling (#889). The removal is complete and coherent. Verified: (a) git ls-files shows no packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/precision or .../api/engine/precision source files remain (only stale untracked __pycache__ dirs on disk); (b) packages/opaque-engine/pyproject.toml:43-52 no longer lists 'opaque.precision*' in [tool.setuptools.packages.find].include; (c) the private statistic itself is gone -- ClippingStats no longer carries all_finite and _all_finite() was deleted from _clipped_fun.py (grep for 'all_finite' over packages/ returns nothing); (d) grep for 'loss_scal|LossScaler|opaque.precision|engine.precision' over packages/, docs/, examples/ finds no library or doc reference; (e) docs/user-guide/precision.md was rewritten (91 lines) and now states 'Opaque does not provide dynamic loss scaling and DPTrainer does not support fp16 training' and 'Opaque therefore does not expose a loss scaler or an aggregate pre-clipping finiteness signal', with a torch.amp compatibility table saying GradScaler has 'No Opaque counterpart. Data-dependent scale adaptation is outside Opaque's accounting model.' No doc still advertises it. (f) Mixed precision still works through the supported route: torch.autocast for bf16 plus the compute_dtype contract; fp16 is refused rather than silently degraded -- _hf_convert.py:350-355 rejects fp16/fp16_full_eval and _training_arguments.py:1442-1443 makes TrainingArguments.fp16 a property that is always False. The ClippingStats dataclass field removal is a breaking API change but ClippingStats is a per-call diagnostic, not serialized state (it is absent from the serialization registry), so there is no state-dict back-compat break.

statuses.title: Per-group clipping crashes DDP training on any partially-empty Poisson round
statuses.note: Fixed by e8568596 fix(clipping): make aux clipping_rate presence track the clipping schema (#875). packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_grad.py:256 now emits 'clipping_rate=None if isinstance(clipping_norm, PerGroup) else 0.0' in _empty_batch_response, and packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py:478 does the same via the factory-time 'is_per_group' flag (_adaptive.py:393). _sync_clipping_rate (_distributed.py:222-249) therefore sees identical presence on every rank. Verified by running the real 2-rank gloo regressions on this tree: packages/opaque-engine/tests/ddp/test_sync_aux_empty_batch.py -> 3 passed (includes the new _worker_per_group_clipped_grad_one_rank_empty_gloo, which builds both ranks' aux through the real clipped_grad(PerGroup, return_aux=True) with rank 0 empty and then calls sync), and packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/ddp/test_dpsgd_cpu_gloo.py -> 6 passed (includes _worker_per_group_adaptive_one_rank_empty_gloo). Both assert a follow-up all_reduce still succeeds, so there is no residual desync. I also checked the sibling clipped_fun path: _compute_clipping_stats (_clipped_fun.py:327-340) returns a per-group dict of zero rates on an empty batch and the ClippedFunAux constructor (_clipped_fun.py:780-785) collapses any dict to None, so empty and non-empty per-group draws agree there too -- no mismatch survives. Residual cosmetic note (not a defect): the older synthetic helper _worker_sync_aux_empty_vs_per_group (engine_ddp_helpers.py:805-849) still hand-builds a per-group rank with clipping_rate=0.5, a float the real per-group path never produces; it now only exercises group_norms presence and the real path is covered by the new helper, so the fix sketch's 'rebuild the helper' step was met by addition rather than by edit.

statuses.title: per_group() silently drops patterns that match no parameter
statuses.note: Fixed by 88f81f2f fix(engine): reject unmatched per-group patterns (#867). packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:140,163-177 now tracks matched_patterns and raises ConfigurationError listing the unmatched patterns plus up to three sample parameter display paths, with an explicit allow_unused_patterns=True escape hatch; the Raises: block (lines 103-109) was updated. Reproduced the original OPQ-332 repro against the current tree: per_group(llama_shaped_params, self_atten=0.1, mlp=2.0, fallback=1.0) now raises ConfigurationError("Patterns did not match any parameter: ['self_atten']. Sample parameter paths: [...]") instead of returning values={'mlp':2.0,'fallback':1.0}; with allow_unused_patterns=True it still degrades as before. The guard is reachable through the trainer: _dp_trainer.py:1541-1546 calls per_group_clipper(trainable_params, fallback=fb, **patterns) with no allow_unused_patterns, so a TrainingArguments.clipping_norm dict with a typo'd or model-mismatched key now fails at trainer construction. docs/user-guide/clipping.md:366-373 documents both the rule and the opt-out. Two doc-level residuals in the same surface are filed as separate low findings (the per_group docstring's own 32-layer example, and the HF trainer doc calling the dict keys 'regex').

statuses.title: Wrapper-blindness survives in unscale_grads and global_norm
statuses.note: Half fixed, half removed. global_norm: 3acdba01 fix(engine): reject unsupported wrapped gradient helpers (#869) added an explicit isinstance guard at packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:377-400 covering ClippedPytree, NoisedPytree, SecondMomentClippingOutput and SecondMomentNoiseOutput, raising InputTypeError that points at .pytree. Reproduced: global_norm(clipped({'g': tensor([3.,4.])}, max_norm=1.0)) now raises InputTypeError instead of returning tensor(0.); it previously returned 0.0. unscale_grads: no longer exists -- its module packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/precision/_loss_scaler.py was deleted by 7f55aae5 (#889), so the second half of OPQ-333 is resolved by removal rather than repair. I checked the remaining internal global_norm call sites (_clipped_fun.py:545 on the raw clip_pytree output, and opaque-auditing _gradient.py:159 on a raw torch.func.grad result) -- neither passes a wrapper, so the new raise is not a regression. One sibling in the same module was not hardened and is filed as a low finding: opaque.pytree.tree_leaves still returns [] for a ClippedPytree.

statuses.title: Empty-batch short-circuit ignores dtype= and pre_clipping_transform structure
statuses.note: Fixed by f59e3c12 fix(clipping): preserve dtype and transform structure in empty-batch short-circuit (#856). The new helper empty_clipped_grads_like (packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_helpers.py:94-127) applies pre_clipping_transform to the zero pytree and then casts leaves to the configured output dtype; it is used by clipped_grad (_clipped_grad.py:232), adaptive_clipped_grad (_adaptive.py:457) and, through clipped_grad, auto_clipped_grad. Reproduced the original failures against the current tree and they are gone: with bf16 params and dtype=torch.float32 the empty and non-empty steps now both return float32 for clipped_grad, auto_clipped_grad and adaptive_clipped_grad; with a structure-changing transform (w -> q) both steps return keys ['q']. Also checked microbatch_size and second_moment=True: both keep the empty/non-empty structure and dtype identical. CAVEAT (filed as finding 'Empty-batch short-circuit applies pre_clipping_transform without NaN/Inf sanitization'): running the user's transform on an all-zero pytree outside the clip_pytree sanitizer makes value-dependent transforms return NaN on empty Poisson rounds, which the pre-fix code (plain zero_grads_like) never did. Verified end to end that the NaN survives gaussian_noise and reaches the optimizer.

statuses.title: fold_in's int/str domain disjointness is not structural
statuses.note: Fixed by e785a9f4 fix(random)!: separate fold-in input domains (#868). packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/random/_engine.py:29-38 now writes a one-byte type tag before each part (b'i' before the 16-byte signed little-endian int, b's' before the UTF-8 string). The two encodings can no longer share a byte stream because the first byte differs, so the disjointness is structural rather than conventional. Reproduced the exact OPQ-335 collision on the current tree: fold_in(key(42), 1).seed = 13284133143826279601 while fold_in(key(42), '\x01' + '\x00'*15).seed = 17548297796905688016 -- they no longer match (the finding recorded both as 2142789487919306769). fold_in(k,1) != fold_in(k,'1') still holds and split(k,n) is still exactly the integer folds. The docstring (lines 68-72) and docs/reference/rng.md:203-205, docs/user-guide/rng-key.md:100-102 were amended to say the separation is enforced by a type tag. The breaking key-derivation change was versioned: _checkpoint.py DP_STATE_BUNDLE_VERSION was bumped (4 -> 5 in this commit, now 8), and _checkpoint.py:399-403 refuses a bundle at a different version. grep confirms _stable_hash64 is the only key-derivation hash in the monorepo (the only other blake2b use is a 48-bit string fingerprint in opaque-optimizers/distributed.py:96, not key material). The cross-package stream-root registry test that the finding referenced was moved out of engine by dd65957d (#884) into tests/integration/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py, where it is broader (15 roots vs 9) and still runs in CI -- .github/workflows/python-tests.yml:89 declares a 'paths: tests' suite. Ran it: 3 passed.

statuses.title: StepPerf.memory_peak_gb on MPS is the run-wide reserved high-water
statuses.note: Fixed by 91f3eb2f fix(profiling): report per-step MPS memory peaks (#866). The misleading contract is gone: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/profiling/_memory.py:265-276 (StepPerf.memory_peak_gb) and :56-66 (MemoryStats) now spell out the CUDA / MPS-with-allocator-stats / MPS-legacy / CPU cases instead of claiming 'Peak GPU memory during the step'. The value is now per-step-scoped on both MPS branches: _capabilities.py:124-139 probes torch.accelerator.memory.memory_stats() for 'allocated_bytes.all.peak' and, when present, get_memory_stats (_memory.py:153-158) reads torch.accelerator.memory.max_memory_allocated and reset_peak_memory (_memory.py:206-210) resets it, so step_perf resets per step (_memory.py:440-441); when absent, step_perf samples torch.mps.current_allocated_memory at entry, every mark and exit (_StepPerfBuilder._sample_peak, _memory.py:339-346) and reports that max with exact_peak=False. step_perf also now drains the device (_sync_device) BEFORE resetting the peak (_memory.py:431-441) so earlier work cannot contaminate the window. Verified the CPU-reachable behavior: the whole engine suite passes (616 passed / 24 skipped, -m 'not cuda and not mps and not slow and not distributed'), including the new test_legacy_mps_peak_is_sampled_per_step and test_synchronizes_before_resetting_peak in tests/profiling/test_step_perf.py and the two _peak_memory_trackable probe tests in tests/device/test_capabilities.py. CAVEAT: I have no Apple Silicon here, so the @pytest.mark.mps branch was verified by reading, not by execution. I checked the one API-availability risk in that branch -- torch.accelerator.memory exists as far back as v2.9.0 (the declared floor in packages/opaque-engine/pyproject.toml:29), confirmed against pytorch/pytorch v2.9.0 torch/accelerator/__init__.py and torch/accelerator/memory.py -- so the uncaught AttributeError I was looking for does not occur on any supported torch; only a RuntimeError from an allocator without stats is possible and that is caught.

findings.title: Empty-batch short-circuit runs pre_clipping_transform on zeros without NaN/Inf sanitization, so value-dependent transforms emit NaN gradients on empty Poisson rounds
findings.claim: The #856 fix for OPQ-334 (commit f59e3c12) made the empty-batch short-circuit call the user's pre_clipping_transform: 'zeros = zero_grads_like(args, argnums); transformed = pre_clipping_transform(zeros)'. On a non-empty step the transform's output passes through clip_pytree, which begins by sanitizing every leaf with torch.nan_to_num(t, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0) (_pytree.py:599-606, and the AUTO-S twin at :463-470). The empty path has no such sanitizer: empty_clipped_grads_like returns the transformed zeros straight into clipped(zeros, max_norm=...). Any transform whose output depends on the gradient values -- the obvious case is a per-example direction/normalization transform, t / global_norm(g) -- evaluates 0/0 on the zero pytree and yields NaN. Before f59e3c12 the empty path was plain zero_grads_like and could not produce a non-finite value, so this is a regression introduced by the fix.
findings.failure_scenario: Functional DP-SGD with Poisson sampling and a normalizing pre_clipping_transform, e.g. tr = lambda g: tree_map(lambda t: t / global_norm(g), g). Reproduced on the current tree (12146ec4): clipped_grad(loss, argnums=0, batch_argnums=(1,2), clipping_norm=1.0, pre_clipping_transform=tr) returns finite gradients on a batch of 4, and tensor([nan, nan, nan]) on the empty draw. auto_clipped_grad(..., R=1.0, pre_clipping_transform=tr) and adaptive_clipped_grad(..., initial_clipping_norm=1.0, pre_clipping_transform=tr) do the same, because all three go through empty_clipped_grads_like. The NaN is not contained: feeding the empty-step ClippedPytree into gaussian_noise(noise_multiplier=1.0) returns tensor([nan, nan, nan]), so the first empty Poisson round permanently NaNs the parameters through the optimizer. The failure is silent -- no warning, no exception -- and the non-empty steps that surround it look healthy, which is precisely the shape the empty-batch short-circuit exists to avoid.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_helpers.py:120-127 -- 'zeros = zero_grads_like(args, argnums); transformed = pre_clipping_transform(zeros); if dtype is None: return transformed; return tree_map(lambda x: x.to(dtype) ..., transformed)' -- no finiteness handling.

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_pytree.py:599-606 -- clip_pytree opens with 'pytree = tree_map(lambda t: torch.nan_to_num(t, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0) if isinstance(t, torch.Tensor) else t, pytree)'; _pytree.py:463-470 is the identical opener in auto_scale_pytree. The non-empty path is sanitized; the empty path bypasses both.
Commit f59e3c12 diff: the old body was 'zeros = zero_grads_like(args, argnums_tuple)' with no transform, so the pre-fix empty path could not emit NaN.

Reproduced (PYTHONPATH into packages/*/src, torch 2.13.0): clipped_grad / auto_clipped_grad / adaptive_clipped_grad each return tensor([nan, nan, nan]) for an empty (0,3) batch with the normalizing transform, and gaussian_noise on that output is also all-NaN, while the same factories on a 4-example batch return finite values.
findings.fix_sketch: Sanitize the empty-batch zeros the same way the non-empty path does: in empty_clipped_grads_like, wrap the transformed tree in torch.nan_to_num(t, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0) before the dtype cast (and do the same for the squared-stream zeros built in _clipped_grad.py:238-245). That keeps the OPQ-334 structure/dtype guarantee while restoring the pre-fix invariant that an empty draw contributes exactly zero. A stricter alternative is to derive the empty output's structure and dtype from the transform without evaluating it on data (e.g. cache the template from the first non-empty step, as empty_collate does) so a value-dependent transform is never called on a synthetic input at all.

findings.title: clipped_fun and auto_clipped_fun, the public power-user primitives, have no empty-batch handling at all and die with an opaque IndexError on a zero-length batch
findings.line: 688 (outputs = vmapped(...) in clipped_fn, no batch_size==0 short-circuit anywhere in the module); packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_auto.py:111 (auto_clipped_fun delegates)
findings.claim: OPQ-334 and its fix (#856) are entirely about clipped_grad's empty-batch short-circuit being structure- and dtype-faithful. The sibling primitives one level down -- clipped_fun and auto_clipped_fun, which packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/fun.py:14-16 advertises as 'stable, supported public API ... for users who need to clip arbitrary per-example outputs or compose custom pipelines' -- have no empty-batch path at all. They call torch.func.vmap directly on a zero-length batch and fail inside vmap. The module that produces the empty batches, packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/functional/_collate.py:4-8, states that empty batches 'arise from any Poisson-style sampler', so the two supported surfaces disagree about whether an empty batch is a supported input.
findings.failure_scenario: A user composes a custom DP pipeline with opaque.api.engine.clipping.fun.clipped_fun (or auto_clipped_fun) plus PoissonSampler and empty_collate, exactly as the collate docstring describes. On the first round where the Poisson draw is empty the loader hands the clip function a zero-length batch and the step dies with 'IndexError: select(): index 0 out of range for tensor of size [0] at dimension 0' raised from inside vmap -- an error that names neither the empty batch nor the API. Reproduced on the current tree for both clipped_fun(f, clipping_norm=1.0, batch_argnums=1) and auto_clipped_fun(f, R=1.0, batch_argnums=1) with a (0,3) batch, while the same calls on a (4,3) batch return correctly. Fail-closed, so no privacy or numerical consequence -- but it aborts training mid-run and the same configuration works through clipped_grad, which is why the inconsistency is a trap rather than a documented limit. This predates the delta; the #856 fix did not extend the empty-batch contract down to these primitives.
evidence: grep for 'numel() == 0|batch_size == 0|is_empty|empty_batch' over packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py returns only line 327, which is inside _compute_clipping_stats (a stats-shaping branch, not a short-circuit); _auto.py has no 'empty' occurrence at all.

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:686-688 -- 'vmapped = _vmap(per_example_fn, in_dims=(None, *in_dims), out_dims=out_dims, randomness="same"); outputs = vmapped(kernel_clipping_norm, *args, **kwargs)' is reached unconditionally.

Contrast packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_grad.py:222-258, where _empty_batch_response exists precisely so 'downstream buffers stay stable across empty and non-empty draws'.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/fun.py:14-16 -- 'These are stable, supported public API'.
Reproduced: both factories raise IndexError('select(): index 0 out of range for tensor of size [0] at dimension 0') on a zero-length batch and succeed on a 4-example batch.
findings.fix_sketch: Give clipped_fun the same guard clipped_grad has: when batch_size_from_args(args, batch_argnums) == 0, skip the vmap and return an empty-batch-shaped output. Because clipped_fun's output structure is fun's, not the parameter pytree's, the template cannot be derived from args -- so either require the caller to supply an out_template= for the empty case, or (cheapest) raise a ConfigurationError naming the empty batch and pointing at clipped_grad, so the limitation is explicit rather than an IndexError from inside vmap. Either way document it in fun.py's module docstring next to the 'stable, supported public API' sentence.

findings.title: tree_leaves still returns [] for a ClippedPytree/NoisedPytree -- the same silent fail-open shape #869 hardened in global_norm, in the same module
findings.claim: 3acdba01 (#869) fixed OPQ-333 by making global_norm raise InputTypeError on the four DP wrapper types, telling the caller to use .pytree. Its immediate neighbour in the same file, tree_leaves, keeps the old behavior: it flattens with optree (for which ClippedPytree is an unregistered frozen dataclass and therefore a single opaque leaf) and then filters with 'isinstance(x, torch.Tensor)', so a wrapper is dropped and the function returns []. The module header even pairs the two -- 'Only tensor leaves are considered for tree_leaves and global_norm' -- so after the fix the file's own stated contract no longer matches one of the two functions it names. tree_flatten, by contrast, returns the wrapper as a leaf, so the three sibling entry points now disagree three ways on the same input.
findings.failure_scenario: A user inspecting DP gradients writes 'total = sum(t.numel() for t in tree_leaves(grads))' or 'max(t.abs().max() for t in tree_leaves(grads))' on the ClippedPytree that clipped_grad returns (the same mental slip OPQ-333 documented for global_norm). tree_leaves returns [], so the sum is 0 and the max raises a bare 'max() arg is an empty sequence' with nothing pointing at the wrapper. Reproduced on the current tree: tree_leaves(clipped({'g': tensor([3.,4.])}, max_norm=1.0)) -> [], while global_norm on the same value now raises InputTypeError and tree_map returns a correctly scaled ClippedPytree. No privacy or numerical consequence -- a monitoring or sizing figure silently reads zero.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:126-127 -- 'flat, _ = _ot.tree_flatten(tree); return [x for x in flat if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor)]'.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:377-400 -- the guard 3acdba01 added, covering ClippedPytree, NoisedPytree, SecondMomentClippingOutput, SecondMomentNoiseOutput.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:16 -- 'Only tensor leaves are considered for tree_leaves and global_norm' (now true of only one of them).

Reproduced side by side on 12146ec4: tree_leaves -> [] ; global_norm -> InputTypeError ; tree_flatten -> ([ClippedPytree(...)], PyTreeSpec(*)) ; tree_map -> ClippedPytree(pytree={'g': tensor([6., 8.])}, max_norm=2.0).
findings.fix_sketch: Mirror the global_norm guard in tree_leaves (and tree_flatten_with_paths, which has the same shape): raise the same InputTypeError naming .pytree when the top-level argument is one of the four wrapper types. Keeping a bare wrapper at the root silently empty is the fail-open the #869 fix set out to remove; nested non-tensor leaves can still be dropped as documented.

findings.title: per_group's own documented example raises for any model with 11 or more layers because substring patterns collide by prefix
findings.line: 116 (Examples block), also 69 and 71 in the module docstring
findings.claim: The Examples block in per_group's docstring -- the file the #867 fix rewrote to document the new unmatched-pattern rule -- ends with '>>> per_group(params, **{f"layers.{i}": norms[i] for i in range(32)})'. Patterns are matched as plain substrings of the leaf's dotted display path ('matches = [pat for pat in all_patterns if pat in display]', _per_group.py:142), so for i >= 10 the pattern 'layers.1' is a substring of the display path 'model.layers.10...'. The parameter then matches two patterns and per_group raises the multi-match ConfigurationError at _per_group.py:155-162. The example therefore cannot work for any transformer with 11+ layers, which is every model family the project supports.
findings.failure_scenario: A user copies the shipped per-layer example to give each layer its own clipping norm on an 8B LLaMA. Reproduced on the current tree with 12 synthetic layers: ConfigurationError("Parameter path ('model.layers.10.mlp.weight') ... matched multiple patterns: ['layers.1', 'layers.10']. Each parameter must match exactly one pattern."). The same call with 10 layers succeeds, so the example looks correct in a small smoke test and fails on the real model. Fail-closed, but the error names neither the substring semantics nor a workaround, and the docstring gives no hint that patterns must be mutually non-prefixing.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:116 -- '>>> per_group(params, **{f\'layers.{i}\': norms[i] for i in range(32)})'.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:142 -- 'matches = [pat for pat in all_patterns if pat in display]' (substring, not regex, not anchored).
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:155-162 -- the multi-match ConfigurationError.
Reproduced: 12-layer params raise the multi-match error on 'model.layers.10.mlp.weight'; the identical call with 10 layers succeeds.
findings.fix_sketch: Change the example to a form that is prefix-free, e.g. '>>> per_group(params, **{f"layers.{i}.": norms[i] for i in range(32)})' (trailing dot) and state in the Args/Notes that patterns are matched as substrings of the dotted display path, so one pattern must not be a prefix of another. Optionally add a construction-time check that no explicit pattern is a substring of another and raise with the trailing-dot suggestion, which turns the confusing per-parameter multi-match error into a single actionable message.

findings.title: DPTrainer documents per-group clipping_norm keys as regex when they are plain substrings, and offers no allow_unused_patterns escape hatch
findings.claim: The trainer documentation says clipping_norm 'accepts a positive scalar (global clipping), a dict keyed by regex on parameter names with a "fallback" entry (per-group clipping)'. The implementation does no regex matching: _dp_trainer.py:1538-1546 strips 'fallback' and forwards the remaining keys verbatim as per_group(**patterns), and per_group matches with 'pat in display' (_per_group.py:142). Per-group clipping norms feed the accountant through PerGroup.effective = sqrt(sum v^2), so which leaves land in which group is sensitivity-relevant, and the doc misdescribes the rule that decides it. The same call site also hard-codes the new strict behavior: it never passes allow_unused_patterns, so the legitimate 'one config across architectures' case that #867 added the flag for is unreachable from DPTrainer.
findings.failure_scenario: A user follows the doc and writes clipping_norm={'model\\.layers\\.\\d+\\.self_attn': 0.1, 'fallback': 1.0}. As a substring that key matches nothing. Before 88f81f2f this degraded silently -- every attention parameter was clipped at the fallback 1.0 instead of 0.1, which is the OPQ-332 defect. After 88f81f2f it raises ConfigurationError at trainer construction, so the outcome is now fail-closed; the residual harm is that the error contradicts the documentation the user was following, and there is no supported way to express a deliberately-partial pattern set from TrainingArguments. Separately, the substring rule quietly widens intent: a doc-following user who writes 'layers.1' expecting an anchored regex match gets every layer whose index starts with 1 (10..19) or, if they also list 'layers.10', the multi-match error.
evidence: docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:92-93 -- 'clipping_norm accepts a positive scalar (global clipping), a dict keyed by regex on parameter names with a "fallback" entry'. Present unchanged at both 4b13d82 (line 84) and 12146ec4 (line 93), so two doc-reconciliation commits in the delta (ba39783d, 12146ec4) passed over it.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1537-1546 -- 'fb = float(mgn["fallback"]); patterns = {k: float(v) for k, v in mgn.items() if k != "fallback"}; ... clip_norm = per_group_clipper(trainable_params, fallback=fb, **patterns)' -- no regex compilation, no allow_unused_patterns.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:142 -- substring matching.
docs/user-guide/clipping.md:365-373 gets it right ('matched by substring against the patterns, using the leaf's display path'), so the two user-facing docs contradict each other.
